### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 471add32df3f89315156cf982586b40e193bb84f`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 471add32df3f89315156cf982586b40e193bb84f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dd8d678dbca047260419b947712700c3e71c44b7` — the merge of head `6aaa0350bb42d2e4de85c8132785f971a24b32e6` into base `471add32df3f89315156cf982586b40e193bb84f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dd8d678dbca047260419b947712700c3e71c44b7 && git checkout dd8d678dbca047260419b947712700c3e71c44b7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 471add32df3f89315156cf982586b40e193bb84f 6aaa0350bb42d2e4de85c8132785f971a24b32e6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 471add32df3f89315156cf982586b40e193bb84f && git merge --no-ff 6aaa0350bb42d2e4de85c8132785f971a24b32e6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 471add32df3f89315156cf982586b40e193bb84f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 471add32df3f89315156cf982586b40e193bb84f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `10142d759859892a248487e0ba3524fcf5aef59f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-execute-transactions.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-hook-dispatch.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-secret-internal-fields.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-defaults-and-autonumbers.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-count-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/external-driver-floor.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts

Ruling applied: the engine hands a data driver the declared `DriverOptionsSchema` keys and nothing else (maintainer, option A); precedent #4400, the closed engine option bags, one hop down. Inputs: the PR body, the file list, the net diff against `main` at this head (origin/main `6d1dc7f835` is 11 commits past the merge-base `1f13eb3189` with no change under `packages/objectql/src` or the two spec files, so the net diff is the PR's diff), and the head's check-runs. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Every driver-hop call site now hands the declared keys and nothing else — correct.** Read at this head, by verb:
   - `find` (engine.ts 6651→6659) and `findOne` (6881→6886): `buildDriverOptions` → local `driverOptions` → the driver.
   - `insert` (8037–8052): one `driverOptions` built from the first row context's bag (plus the derived organization), handed to `encryptSecretFields` (8079) and through it to the `sys_secret` create (engine-secret-internal-fields.ts 333, `one.driverOptions`), to `issueAutonumbers` (8323, 8399), to `bulkCreate` / `create` (8382, 8385), and to `createWithAutonumberResync` (8410 → engine-defaults-and-autonumbers.ts 754, 766, 792, 810).
   - `update`: the pre-read `preOpts` (9485→9493) is built from the caller's bag and so is declared-only; `driverOptions` (9662) reaches `encryptSecretFields` (9783, 10210), `updateByIdExpecting` (10127 → engine-insert.ts 176–180: `update`, `updateMany`, the `findOne` readback), `update` (10128), the two pre-reads (10561, 10575) and `updateMany` (10578).
   - `delete`: the pre-reads (11552, 11717); `driverOptions` (11739) reaches the two pre-reads (11844, 11852) and `deleteMany` (11854); the by-id path (11784–11787) and the batched predicate path (11868, 11886) rebuild through `buildDriverOptions` from the merged hook view, which the pick cuts to the declared set again.
   - `count` (engine-count-aggregate.ts 146–155) and `aggregate` (engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts 523, 567) build from an `undefined` base — already closed before this PR, unchanged.
   - raw `execute` (engine-execute-transactions.ts 132): `pickDeclaredDriverOptions(options)`.
   - The secret helper's own reads and the handle release build fresh `{ transaction }` bags (engine-secret-internal-fields.ts 385–392, `privilegedReadDriverOptions` at 543, 586) — declared-only by construction.
   - A grep of `driver.<verb>(` over `packages/objectql/src` at this head finds no call that is handed `hookContext.input.options`, `optionsBase` or a caller `options` bag; the three sites that did (engine.ts 6647, 6872, 10108 and the four pre-reads on `main`) are the ones the diff cuts. The new test drives every verb with a bag carrying engine-level keys and asserts `Reflect.ownKeys` of what the driver receives is a subset of the declared set, with a non-vacuity check that each driver method was reached.
2. **Declared keys are read off the schema shape, tombstones excluded — correct.** `declaredDriverOptionKeys()` reads `DriverOptionsSchema.shape` (a resolving access on the `lazySchema` proxy) and drops a member that admits only absence by walking `_zod.def` through `optional` / `nullable` / `default` / `readonly` to `never`. `retiredKey()` is `z.never({ error }).optional()` (retired-key.ts 194), so `timeout` is out and the nine live keys are in. Test case 1 pins both directions: whatever is excluded refuses every probe value, and the six engine-threaded keys are present. The memo is process-lifetime on a module constant — fine.
3. **`transaction` / `tenantId` / `tenantIds` / `timezone` / `preserveAudit` / `bypassTenantAudit` still arrive — correct.** `buildDriverOptions` (engine-driver-options.ts 259–309) fills each in only when the declared pick left it `undefined`, exactly the pre-PR fill-in rule, so a caller's explicit value still wins; the control block pins arrival on every verb and the explicit `bypassTenantAudit` / `preserveAudit` values unchanged.
4. **The after-hook view stays additive — correct.** `mergeDriverOptionsIntoHookView` answers `{ ...bag, ...driverOptions }`, or the caller's own bag when nothing is added; `find`, `findOne`, `update` and `delete` assign it to `input.options` after the build, `insert` assigns it to every row context (8049–8052). Bulk per-row `afterUpdate` / `afterDelete` contexts copy `batchCtx.input.options` after that assignment (engine-hook-dispatch.ts 98–104). plugin-audit's `writeCommentMentions` (`afterInsert` / `afterUpdate`, audit-writers.ts 2646) reads the caller's `onMentionsWithheld` off `ctx.input.options` and still finds it; the third test block pins that and the `afterFind` case. Trigger order: `beforeFind` (6648, 6879), `beforeInsert` (7605), `beforeUpdate` (9409) and `beforeDelete` (11644) all fire before their verb's build, and no hook fires between the build and the verb's driver calls, so a `before*` write to a declared key still reaches the driver and a write to an undeclared key does not — the ruling's intent.
5. **The symbol key is gone from the driver bag and its one reader still gets it — correct.** `WRITE_PRECONDITION_OPTION` is read off the caller's bag at engine.ts 8781 into `opCtx.writePrecondition` before the build and handed to `updateByIdExpecting` as the explicit `precondition` argument (10125–10127); `pickDeclaredDriverOptions` iterates declared string keys only, so no symbol reaches a driver; the only producer is engine-insert.ts 196 and the only reader is 8781. The hook view keeps it (object spread copies own enumerable symbols).
6. **Check-runs on the head (gate verdicts, read from the API, not the seat).** Every completed run is `success` or `skipped`: Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Type Check · source / consumer / debt / workspace, Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Lint UI (skipped), Type Check UI, Test UI 1–16/16, Test Core 1–8/8, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate. Polled 2026-11-04T17:00:25Z: every check-run completed, none with a conclusion other than `success` or `skipped`.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql` **patch**, `Clause-②: no` with no arm, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and no spec changeset — **consistent with the diff.**

AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 is the text: "`Clause-②: yes|no` plus at most one arm from the closed pair `(widening)`/`(narrowing)` (`(narrowing)` is BREAKING, `no (widening)` malformed), and `Metadata-protocol: added|narrowed|semantic|none`, the change to what a metadata author can write … The level follows the kind alone: a kind takes at least **`minor`** on a package the diff moves, `none` takes **`patch`**; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition." The gate's own reading of the value (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`): `Clause-②: no` means "this PR widens no published accept set or public surface; add `(narrowing)` if it narrows one".

The dev's question 2 — does dropping keys a third-party driver could read only with a cast count as narrowing — **no.** The published surface at the hop is the `IDataDriver` contract: every method takes `options?: DriverOptions` (contracts/data-driver.ts 108–269), and that type declares none of the dropped keys; a read of one was never on the published surface, so no published accept set or public surface narrows. The engine's own doors accept exactly the bags they accepted (`ENGINE_FIND/UPDATE/DELETE_OPTION_KEYS` unchanged); nothing an author writes changes. What does change is runtime behaviour for a reader outside its contract, which is the changeset's "Who moves" paragraph to carry — and it does — not a `(narrowing)` arm. No ADR-0087 disposition is owed. The spec edits are comment-only: no `.describe()`, no export, and the edited `hook.zod.ts` paragraph feeds no generated page (`content/docs/references` carries none of its sentences), so no regenerated artifact and no spec changeset is owed; the type-check lanes that carry the spec gates are green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **(1) Silent drop versus a dev-mode warn — the silent drop holds; no warn.** Every caller bag carries engine-level keys on every call (the doors' legal sets include them by design), so a warn keyed on "undeclared key dropped at the hop" would fire on every verb call and train readers to skim it (AGENTS.md, degradation log levels); nothing is lost — the engine reads those keys itself, and the bag was already judged at the engine's own door (#4400). A warn would be meaningful only if keyed on what a driver actually reads, which the engine cannot see. The contract is pinned by the test, which is the right instrument. Decided; nothing to raise.
- **(3) The objectstack-ai/cloud driver census — landing does not wait for it; it is a pre-release item.** The repository is not readable from this session either (GET refused; not attached). Reasons landing is independent of it: the ruling is the maintainer's; the in-repo contract never declared the keys; cloud consumes `@objectstack/objectql` at its own pinned upgrade, where its driver suites run against the new hop; and the migration is one sentence — declare the key on `DriverOptionsSchema` first, a spec change with its own review. Before the release that carries this patch: a cloud-side census card, written at rule level (undeclared keys), per security-findings §4 — one line on any public surface. Prime Directive #15 keeps the release itself with the maintainer.
- **Out-of-scope note (the insert option bag has no unknown-key door) — accurate, correctly out of scope.** `rejectUnknownEngineOptions` runs for `find` (engine.ts 6538), `findOne` (6797), `update` (8717) and `delete` (11348) and never for `insert`; so an undeclared insert option is still ignored at the engine door, the exact #4400 shape, and after this PR also never reaches a driver. A card under the #4400 precedent (PD #10), not this PR. One consequence for the prose face, for the seat's ACCEPT: the changeset line "The schema's other declared keys pass when a caller sets them" is true at `insert` and `execute` only — on the four doored verbs the door refuses `timeoutMs` / `skipCache` / `traceContext` before the hop (`ENGINE_DRIVER_PASSTHROUGH_KEYS`, engine-top-level.ts 284–286, admits the six threaded keys only). **should-fix** (prose): qualify that sentence.
- **Security-findings §6 (disclosure).** Title, PR body, changeset, the six commit messages and every test name stay at rule level — "the declared driver options and nothing else", "undeclared keys" — and no mechanism is narrated. Two wordings to tighten, **should-fix**: the body's and changeset's "What stays with the engine" bullet and commit `de02e50287`'s first line enumerate categories and one key of the undeclared set; say "undeclared keys". The four re-pointed `engine.test.ts` assertions name one undeclared key in the negative; assert against `declaredDriverOptionKeys()` (the subset form the new test uses) instead. No `security-note.md` or similar is in the file list.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login note owed.

### ④ Design judgment

- **`driver.zod.ts` (hits).** The added paragraph states what the code now does: the engine hands a driver the keys declared here, retired tombstones aside, whatever else rode in the caller's bag, and a key a driver needs is declared here first — `pickDeclaredDriverOptions` and `admitsOnlyAbsence` are exactly that, and the test's first case holds the schema and the code to each other. Holds against its first consumer. (The docblock sits above the trailing `import` rather than on the export — pre-existing placement, not this PR's.)
- **`hook.zod.ts` (hits).** The PHASE sentence is true for both phases: a `before*` handler reads the caller's bag (every `before*` trigger precedes its verb's build, ① item 4); an `after*` handler reads the merged view, which is additive and strips nothing (`{ ...bag, ...driverOptions }`); and the new sentence "the merged view is the hooks', not the driver's" is what every verb now does. **should-fix**: the parenthetical still says the merge is done by `buildDriverOptions` ("merges the driver-facing keys onto it (`buildDriverOptions`: …)"); at this head `buildDriverOptions` produces the driver's set and `mergeDriverOptionsIntoHookView` does the merge — name both so the sentence points at the code that does it. `hook-input-shape-contract.test.ts` pins the envelope rows and is unaffected.
- **Break attempts.**
  - *A driver call site still passing the raw bag:* none at this head (① item 1 lists every site, the helpers included).
  - *A hook mutating `input.options` after the split and expecting the driver to see it:* no hook fires between any verb's build and its driver calls, and the two `delete` paths that rebuild from the merged view pass through the pick again. **should-fix** (robustness, not a hole today): `mergeDriverOptionsIntoHookView(undefined, d)` answers `d` itself, so when a caller passes no bag (`update` / `delete` with `options` undefined) the hooks' view and the driver's bag are one object, while the docblock promises the driver "is handed `driverOptions` itself" as a thing apart; answer `{ ...driverOptions }` so a later reordering of a hook and a driver call cannot reopen the door.
  - *A remote / wire driver path:* a plugin-published external driver sits behind `createExternalDriverFloor`, which forwards `options` to the inner driver unchanged and adds no key (external-driver-floor.ts 224–261); the cut is upstream in the engine, so a floored driver receives the declared set. The in-repo wire driver (`driver-odata`) and the five other drivers read only `transaction`, `tenantId`, `tenantIds`, `timezone` and `bypassTenantAudit` off their `DriverOptions` argument (census over `packages/drivers/*/src`). Direct `getDriver()` calls by plugins are outside the engine hop and the ruling; unchanged.
  - *A second key list:* `ENGINE_DRIVER_PASSTHROUGH_KEYS` (engine-top-level.ts 284–286) is the doors' admit list, held to the `Engine*OptionsSchema` shapes by `engine-unknown-option.test.ts`; it is not a restatement of the hop's set and the two stay consistent. **should-fix**: its docblock ("the option bag IS the base of the driver options") now reads "the bag's declared keys are the base".

No must-fix. Four should-fix items (the `hook.zod.ts` parenthetical, the merge helper's no-bag copy, the pass-through docblock, the disclosure wording), one prose qualification for the seat's ACCEPT.

The body states the hardening rule ("the declared driver options and nothing else"), "undeclared keys", and names no mechanism; the two sentences that enumerated categories are gone (① item 1).
